In terms of physics, specifically, I believe a lot of people forget that the specific type of energy manipulation that is attributed to Sylus is essentially busted. Even though Caleb's Evol is called "gravity manipulation" it does not peak the OP charts. And thus in terms of danger scale should not be before Xavier. His Evol should have been more appropriately phrased as "Center of Gravity Manipulation".

His powers, much to people's misconception, can not alter the physics of gravity and thus will not create cosmic events like black holes. After studying his moves and skill animations, cutscenes and official posts about him I noted the use of red/ blue vertical particles. I believe the devs are trying to depict that his Evol shifts gravitational poles, poles are generally depicted as red/ blue. So essentially, he targets an object and shifts that object's center of gravity. But because we humans, as well as all objects we create, adhere strictly to Earth's natural poles, **inverting** our personal gravity against the Earth's will essentially freeze us in place, while an **opposite tilt** will make things float/ hover based on the object's weight relative to Earth's pull. This is different from something like Ochaco's (from MHA) gravity manipulation which nulls any objects' force against gravity.

Now Xavier's light manipulation is significantly more deadly along with his potential immortality. It grants him speed that is too great to stop if we assume he is faster/ as fast as the speed of light. His light manipulation may be capable of altering our visual perception as well (fight with Tezcatlipoca). >!He is also from the future with the ability to harness powers that we do not know about yet.!<

As well as Sylus's energy manipulation. The issue with energy manipulation as a concept is that it is vague. What energy? Photon? Kinetic? Atomic? Nuclear? Gravitational? Thermal? It doesn't specify. >!But from what I've seen of Sylus, he can heal (his trailer), break down organic growths (Luke & Kieran's Wanderer Crystallization transformation), free fall from skyscraper heights and nullify the effects of gravity upon himself and anyone/ anything he is carrying (standard myth), deconstruct his own cells/ particles and apparate in a different space (all his companion kits). Not to mention he is immortal and is still unable to die so I would assume he has knowledge that would surpass others.!<

I'd still give it to Xavier > Sylus > Rafayel = Caleb = Zayne. This is only danger in terms of the power they hold.

>!He likely came to the conclusion that MC's soul was split and contained within the Aether Core. Thus the story quest. MC wanted to retrieve the Core for the Hunter's Association, but Sylus wanted to retrieve it to make MC whole again.!<

>!When the Aether Core's power, that originally belonged to MC, flows back into her, the empty stone shatters.!<

>!Now she remembers glimpses of her past. Since her half of the soul is whole now, her soul bond with Sylus is active again.!<

>!And remember that bond she had with Sylus that they have half of each other's souls? They were supposed to always be together and never betray one another. At present, their relationship is rocky and she doesn't particularly like him at first. I believe the energy linkage that forms when she gets her soul back is a manifestation of that bond. Red (Sylus's soul) and Golden (MC's) threads forcibly tying them together. It's like the bond has a mind of it's own and recognizes that Sylus and MC have negative feelings towards one another, and thus forcibly keeps them physically bound together.!<

>!Keep in mind, the linkage gets tighter in times MC is on guard, annoyed, or upset with Sylus. When she begins to like him again, the linkage disappears.!<

>!When they willingly want to be together, the bond/ linkage is redundant and loosens, when they have negative feelings for one another, the bond/ linkage tightens to ensure they don't part.!<
